newsitem.title: USA: U.S. blue chips slide, NYSE sets trading curbs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. blue chips slide, NYSE sets trading curbs.

text.p: U.S. blue chip shares tumbled on Wednesday following a slump in the bond market and on profit-taking after the Federal Reserve decided to leave short-term interest rates unchanged.
The Dow industrial average was down about 57 points to 7247, prompting the New York stock Exchange to set curbs on index-arbitrage trading. Earlier in the day it touched a session high of about 7353.
The long bond traded off 28/32 at a 6.98 percent yield, well below intraday highs. But the Nasdaq composite stayed firm, up seven points to around 1371 as tech stocks rose.
